title: When Screens Become a Battlefield: How Do We Protect Our Children from Cyberbullying?
summary:
Imagine your child, aged 10-12, comes home from school and is enjoying time playing on their tablet or phone. Suddenly, their expression changes, their smile freezes, and signs of worry or sadness appear on their face. They might not talk about it immediately, but you sense something isn't right. Is it just a minor disagreement with a friend? Or is something deeper and more painful happening in their digital world?

Cyberbullying isn't just a fleeting joke or a momentary disagreement; it's a specter that haunts our children everywhere and at all times. Unlike traditional bullying, which ends when the school day is over, cyberbullying remains present 24/7, infiltrating the privacy of their homes, and its digital traces are etched forever. This continuous and widespread nature makes it more painful and harder to deal with, as it threatens their psychological well-being and affects their sense of security even in their own homes.

Our mission as parents is to be a shield and a fortress for our children. Teach your child that their role is not just a bystander, but a change-maker. Encourage them not to participate in any form of bullying, even if it's just by liking or re-sharing. Train them to take a screenshot of any harmful content, then report it to the relevant platform, and most importantly, to come directly to you to tell you what happened. In serious cases, always remember that there are specialized official bodies in your country that can deal with cybercrimes.
try_this: Tonight: Talk to your child about a hypothetical scenario: "If you saw cyberbullying happening to your close friend, what would you do?" And train them on the practical steps: screenshot the content → report to the platform → tell me immediately.
reflection_prompts: Has your child ever experienced cyberbullying or witnessed a similar situation before?
Does your child know how to report cybercrimes to the official authorities in your country if necessary?
